title: When Can LLM Digital Twins Reduce Human Measurement? From Behavioral Fidelity to Statistical Substitutability
abstract: arXiv:2609.07987v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based digital twins promise to reduce repeated human data collection by generating person- specific responses, yet existing evaluations provide little evidence about whether they can reduce human measurement while preserving valid inference. To address this, we introduce statistical substitutability, an inferential criterion that evaluates the extent to which twin predictions can reduce human measurement for a particular estimand while preserving valid inference. We develop a framework, grounded in mixed-subject and prediction-powered inference, that evaluates statistical substitutability along four dimensions: aggregate fidelity, paired respondent-level signal, finite-sample human-label recovery, and stability across populations. translated_title: LLM数字孪生何时能减少人类测量？从行为保真度到统计可替代性
translated_abstract: 基于LLM的数字孪生有望通过生成针对特定个体的响应来减少重复的人类数据收集，然而现有评估几乎没有提供证据表明它们能否在保持有效推断的同时减少对人类测量的依赖。为解决这一问题，我们引入了统计可替代性这一推断准则，用于评估在保持有效推断的前提下，孪生预测能够针对特定估计目标在多大程度上减少人类测量。我们开发了一个基于混合被试设计和预测驱动推断的框架，从四个维度评估统计可替代性：总体保真度、配对的个体层面信号、有限样本下人类标签的恢复能力，以及跨人群的稳定性。在涵盖行为实验、多个模型和替代性被试表示的两项实证评估中，我们发现数字孪生能够再现人类的平均效应，同时提供（原文摘要此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出“统计可替代性”这一新的推断准则及四维评估框架，系统回答了LLM数字孪生何时能在保持有效统计推断的前提下真正替代人类测量，并发现其虽能再现平均人类效应，但要实现个体层面的可替代性仍面临更严格的要求。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "statistical substitutability" as a new inferential criterion with a four-dimension evaluation framework to determine when LLM digital twins can genuinely reduce human measurement while preserving valid inference, finding that although twins can reproduce average human effects, respondent-level substitutability faces stricter requirements.
